# strataglyph

The Strataglyph runner. It runs on your own computer, takes build jobs from
your Strataglyph specifications, and builds them as code with the coding
agent you already use: Claude Code, Codex or OpenCode. It pushes each job to a
`strataglyph/` branch of your repository and never force-pushes.

## Install

Node 24 or newer is needed, as the coding agents need too.

```sh
npm install -g strataglyph
```

Or run it without installing:

```sh
npx strataglyph runner --server https://your-strataglyph.example
```

## Sign in

```sh
strataglyph runner --server https://your-strataglyph.example
```

The first run shows a code. Open Build › Runners and servers in Strataglyph,
choose Connect a runner and enter the code. The runner then acts as you. The
address is remembered, so later runs only need `strataglyph runner`.

## Where it works

It works where you start it. Start it inside your clone of a project's
repository and it works in that clone: each job gets a git worktree in
`.strataglyph/` at the top of your clone, named after its branch, so
`git branch` lists the `strataglyph/` branches and you can open their files
in place. The run's own branch gets one worktree, kept for the run and belonging
to the runner that first merges into it, while a read-only stage works in a copy
of its own. Your own working tree,
current branch and uncommitted changes are never touched, and `.strataglyph/`
is kept out of `git status`.

For any other project it serves, it keeps a clone in a folder of its own
inside the folder you started it in (in `.strataglyph/` when that is a clone).
`--dir` chooses another folder. Its worktrees go in `.strataglyph/` at the top
of that clone as well, never beside it. A job's folder stays while its run is
open, so you can look at its work, and the runner prints where it is. A merge
outside a run starts again from `origin/<branch>` in a fresh folder each time,
so it never merges onto an old commit. The runner removes only the folders it
made and marked, and only when the same factory next runs. A folder it didn't
mark is left alone; when it has the name a branch wants, the runner works in
the next free name beside it.

## Pull requests

If GitHub's `gh` command is installed and signed in, the runner also looks up
each build's pull request and its checks, read-only, with your own sign-in. It
never comments, merges or closes anything.

## Labels

A runner can carry labels, such as `rust`, `linux-arm64` or `gpu`. Work that
needs labels only goes to a runner that has all of them, and work no runner
online can take says which label is missing.

Set them on the runner's card in Build › Runners and servers, or when you
start it:

```sh
strataglyph runner --label rust --label gpu
STRATAGLYPH_LABELS=rust,gpu strataglyph runner
```

Labels given when it starts replace the ones set on its card, each time it
starts. Without them, the card's labels are kept.

## On a server

A server runner belongs to the organization, not to a person. An owner or
admin adds it with the code it shows, and it acts as the organization: it
serves only that organization's projects, takes any of its jobs and uses the
git access set up on its machine, such as a deploy key. The coding agents use
keys set up on the machine; Strataglyph never sees, stores or sends them.

It runs unattended with `--service`: it never asks for anything, and after an
error it waits and starts again. It stops for good, with exit code 78, only
when its sign-in was removed or it needs updating. Build › Runners and
servers › Add a server shows these steps with your address filled in.

On Linux with systemd:

```sh
# 1. Install the runner, with Node 24+, git and a coding agent installed for every user
sudo npm install -g strataglyph

# 2. A user of its own
sudo useradd --system --create-home --home-dir /var/lib/strataglyph --shell /usr/sbin/nologin strataglyph

# 3. Git access: add the printed key as a deploy key with write access
sudo -u strataglyph -H mkdir -p -m 700 /var/lib/strataglyph/.ssh
sudo -u strataglyph -H ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -N "" -f /var/lib/strataglyph/.ssh/id_ed25519
sudo cat /var/lib/strataglyph/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub

# 4. The agents' keys, such as ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=..., one per line
sudo install -d -m 755 /etc/strataglyph
sudo install -m 640 -g strataglyph /dev/null /etc/strataglyph/runner.env
sudoedit /etc/strataglyph/runner.env

# 5. Sign in once: an owner or admin enters the code in Add a server. Then press Ctrl+C.
sudo -u strataglyph -H strataglyph runner --service --sign-in --server https://your-strataglyph.example --dir /var/lib/strataglyph/work
```

Then add `/etc/systemd/system/strataglyph-runner.service`:

```ini
[Unit]
Description=Strataglyph runner
Wants=network-online.target
After=network-online.target

[Service]
Type=simple
User=strataglyph
Group=strataglyph
WorkingDirectory=/var/lib/strataglyph
Environment=HOME=/var/lib/strataglyph
EnvironmentFile=-/etc/strataglyph/runner.env
ExecStart=/usr/bin/env strataglyph runner --service --server https://your-strataglyph.example --dir /var/lib/strataglyph/work
Restart=always
RestartSec=10
RestartPreventExitStatus=78
KillMode=mixed
TimeoutStopSec=5min

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
```

And start it:

```sh
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable --now strataglyph-runner
journalctl -u strataglyph-runner -f
```

## Use

```sh
strataglyph runner            # take jobs until stopped
strataglyph runner agents     # which coding agents this computer has
strataglyph runner --sign-in  # sign in again, such as after removing it
strataglyph --version
```

Options:

- `--dir <folder>`: where it keeps its clones (default: the folder it's started in)
- `--quiet`: only say when each job starts and ends, not every step
- `--json`: one JSON object per line, for scripts
- `--jobs <n>`: stop after n jobs
- `--label <label>`: a label, such as `rust`; repeat it for more
- `--service`: run unattended as a system service

Press Ctrl+C once to finish the current job and stop, twice to stop at once.

## Start a project from a specification

```sh
strataglyph init --spec <name> [folder]       # bring the specification here, linked
strataglyph init --spec <name> --with-code    # and clone the code it names
```

`init` writes the specification's whole project (its `piton.config.pi`, `tethers/` and source) into a new folder named after it, or the folder you give, and links it so `spec pull` and `spec push` work at once. It builds the guidance for the coding agents it finds on your computer when `piton` is installed; `--agent claude-code,codex` chooses them.

Run inside a clone of the code, or with `--with-code`, the specification sits beside the code but stays out of the code's git: it is listed in `.git/info/exclude`, and a pre-commit hook refuses any commit that holds it. Never run `git clean -x` there, since it deletes ignored files; `strataglyph spec restore` brings the specification back, though edits you never pushed are lost.

Older projects are moved over when you ask:

- A repository that commits its specification with the code: `strataglyph spec separate` takes it out of git (staged for you to commit), and `--undo` puts it back.
- A project that tethered the specification and built on it: `strataglyph init --spec <name>` inside it offers to make the two one specification, sent as a branch for review; `strataglyph init --undo-move` puts it back.

## Specifications on your computer

Run these inside a Piton project, with the runner signed in as you:

```sh
strataglyph spec pull                         # bring the main specification here
strataglyph spec push [--merge]               # send your edits to a branch of yours
strataglyph spec tether --spec <name> [--as <package>]
```

`spec tether` imports a specification into another project with `piton tether`, under the package name set on its Dashboard in Use in another project. To let `piton tether` and `piton update` fetch it again later, let git use the runner's sign-in once:

```sh
git config --global credential.https://<your-strataglyph>.helper "!strataglyph git-credential"
```
